findings.summary: Nothing the practice works on is ever identified or counted: no patent or application number, no mark, product, cited reference or examiner, and no count of families or references, so an IP practice's files read as if redacted.
findings.evidence: d:0008, a partner recommending a fee payment: 'My recommendation is to pay the maintenance fee on the older patent now.' (no patent number, fee window or amount). d:0034's 'Position by Application' table has rows 'Earliest application', 'Second application', 'Application closest to allowance', 'Remaining designated applications' where a real report lists serial numbers. The Jackson trademark clearance never names the mark it is clearing in any of its nine documents (d:0043: 'whether the name it proposes to adopt can be used and registered'). d:0017 promises 'I will give you a count once the screen is complete'; the count never arrives (d:0022: 'most search results were set aside'). Prior art is 'the second reference' (d:0033). The five onboarding records give no USPTO registration number or bar admission for any hire. The report's unowned-number count of 0 is this omission, not a virtue, for a patent firm.

findings.summary: No email, letter, memo or set of minutes shows a docket or matter number, though the firm's own documents say every client update cites one, and no memo, minutes or status report states its own date.
findings.evidence: d:0063: routine news 'reaches the client as a short email that cites the docket number'; d:0007 and d:0037 say the same; d:0011: office action decisions will go 'with the docket number in the subject line'. Every rendered client email subject is the bare engagement title, e.g. 'Subject: RE: Trademark Clearance for Jackson Inc' (d:0049), and letter Re: lines carry no 'Our Ref'. Kickoff memos open 'To: ... From: ... Matter: Patent Portfolio Review for Odonnell Inc' with no Date line (d:0005; same in d:0016, d:0031, d:0044, d:0055); minutes such as d:0050 ('Working Session: Trademark Clearance for Jackson Inc') never state the meeting date, which exists only in the filename.

findings.summary: The firm has no location: all five engagement letters choose 'the law of the state in which our office is located' without naming the state, the letterhead carries only a web address, and the overviews' contact sections give no address, phone or email.
findings.evidence: d:0054: 'governed by the law of the state in which our office is located ... brought in the state or federal courts sitting in that state'; d:0004 and d:0043: 'the law of the state in which this firm maintains its principal office'; d:0015 and d:0030 use the same circumlocution. No lawyer drafts a governing-law clause that way. The rendered d:0004 letterhead is 'Hollowell Patent Group PLLC www.hollowellpatent.com' and its inside address is 'Gary Smith / General Manager / Odonnell Inc' with no street. d:0063's 'How to reach us' section says only that Mary Bradley 'handles inquiries about new matters'; d:0037's 'Contact' section likewise names her with no means of reaching her.

findings.summary: In each of the three five-message client threads the final reply regresses against the history quoted directly beneath it, reporting as news a stage the thread passed days earlier and asking again for what was already supplied.
findings.evidence: Jackson: d:0045 (May 7) 'with your approval we ordered the full search. Its report came back late last week, and Kelly is now reviewing it'; d:0049 (May 10, quoting it) 'Further to the note below, the screening searches on the candidate marks are complete. We have ordered full searches ... and we will start our review as soon as the reports come back', and the one proposed name has silently become several 'candidate marks'. Price-Henson: d:0056 (Apr 11) 'we are reading them now' and 'The drawings your engineering team sent were enough to start charting'; d:0060 (Apr 16) 'To move from collecting the record to reading it, we need ... A product description or data sheet', ignoring the engineer call arranged in d:0057-d:0059. FTO: d:0017 'The screen is about a third done'; d:0021 'the search is finished and screening has started', then explains the screening stages afresh. In all three, the final message was authored in a later work order (author-0005/0009/0011) than messages 1-4 (author-0004/0008/0010).

findings.summary: The managing partner's five engagement letters share no firm form: standard terms are redrafted in each, and the liability clause flips between disclaiming any limit and capping liability at fees paid.
findings.evidence: d:0004 (2019): 'Nothing in this letter limits our liability to the company for our own professional negligence. The rules of professional conduct do not permit a lawyer to limit that liability in advance unless the client has separate counsel'; d:0015 (2020): 'our liability arising out of this engagement is limited to the fees paid under it'; d:0030 (2021): 'the firm's total liability arising out of this engagement will not exceed the fees the company has paid'; d:0054 (2025): 'This letter does not limit our liability for our own professional negligence.' Payment terms move between 'payable within thirty days' (d:0004, d:0043) and 'due on receipt' (d:0030, d:0054), and the same clause is retitled 'Governing Law', 'Applicable Law', 'Choice of Law and Forum'. A ten-person firm runs these terms off one template; the per-letter variation reads as the voice-diversify instruction reaching boilerplate it should have left alone.

findings.summary: Who writes what is inverted: non-attorney patent agents issue four of the five kickoff memos assigning work to partners and associates, while a partner or the managing partner writes seven of the nine sets of minutes with juniors in the room.
findings.evidence: d:0016 'From: Richard Henderson' (patent agent) directs the supervising partner: 'Heather: confirm how we treat applications that publish after the search closes'. d:0044 'From: Ashley Williams, Patent Agent' to the Managing Partner and an Associate assigns the trademark memorandum to the associate, while noting 'our registration does not extend to trademark matters'. d:0010 'Recorded by Heather Munoz.' with a patent agent and an associate present; d:0050 'Minutes taken by Mary Bradley' with an associate and a patent agent attending. The two sets kept by the associate (d:0033 'Joseph Walker, Associate (notes)', d:0035) show the ordinary pattern.

findings.summary: The doctrinal and procedural content is accurate for the genre and the year, so the defects above are structural omissions, not domain ignorance.
findings.evidence: Revival of a lapsed patent requires a statement 'that the delay was unintentional' (d:0008); an unrecorded assignment 'remains valid between the inventor and the company. It is exposed against a later purchaser' (d:0011); engineers' emails on third-party patents 'can be produced in litigation and read as knowledge of the patent' (d:0018); a terminally disclaimed continuation is 'enforceable only while the two remain commonly owned' (d:0061); file histories downloaded 'from Patent Center' in 2025 (d:0055); 2020 working sessions 'held by video conference' (d:0022).
